quotes: Key rotation is already implemented in this checkout, with support added in ItsDangerous 2.0. You can use it without adding a Signer parameter.
signer = Signer(["old-key", "new-key"])  # oldest to newest ... new_token = signer.sign(b"user-id=42")  # signed with new-key
Flask 3.1+ supports rotation for its built-in cookie sessions through SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS
Extensions that use SECRET_KEY may need separate support, so check your session implementation and extensions too.
Keep the old key available until sessions signed with it have expired or been reissued with the new key.

X.actionable: yes: use the list or SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS and check the Flask version instead of patching Signer. It misses the 3.1.0 bug and never mentions keeping salt and algorithm unchanged.

quotes: key rotation already exists in this checkout, so you don't need a new Signer parameter.
Pass keys to the existing secret_key argument oldest to newest. New signatures use the last key; verification accepts any listed key.
Flask's built-in cookie sessions support SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS ... This option was added in Flask 3.1. Use 3.1.1 or later
Extensions and custom session backends need separate checking.
Decide how long to retain old keys based on session lifetime and refresh behavior; keeping a key accepts signatures made with it.

why: Both catch the main traps equally (both only hint at extension scope). Y's citations are all correct, it flags the Flask 3.1.0 key-selection advisory, and it gives a concrete integration-test first step. X has one wrong test line reference.
